A Lebenslauf is personal data, and the law gives you three things because of it: to see what is held, to take a copy with you, and to have it deleted. All three are here.
Written into the documents of the app exactly as the server holds it, and then handed on, so you can keep it where you like.
Delete the account and everything in it

What you entered about yourself, the documents on file, the postings you pasted and every application are deleted from the server. This cannot be undone. Bewerbo then opens an empty account, so you can begin again.
These terms hold between you and the operator named in the Impressum for as long as you use Bewerbo. Using the app means accepting them.

What Bewerbo does: it turns the profile you enter into a German Lebenslauf and Anschreiben and exports them as one PDF. It is a writing aid. It does not apply on your behalf, it does not deal with an employer for you, and it cannot promise that an application succeeds.

What you enter stays yours, and it is yours to get right. The app lays out what you write; it cannot know whether it is true. A statement in a Lebenslauf that does not hold is a matter between you and the employer.
The German may be written by a language model. Read it before you send it. What a foreign qualification counts for here is written into a document only after you have confirmed it yourself.

The app costs nothing and is provided as it is. The operator answers without limit for intent, for gross negligence and for injury to life, body or health; beyond that only for breaking an obligation this agreement stands on, and then only for the damage such use typically causes.
You can delete your account at any time, on the settings screen, and that ends this agreement. The operator may close an account used to attack or abuse the service.
Responsible for what happens to your data is the operator named in the Impressum, where you also find how to reach them.

Held are: what you enter about yourself — name, address, telephone, e-mail, date of birth, the jobs you have held, what you studied, your languages and the reasons you gave for gaps; for each document on file its title, kind and number of pages; the postings you paste in; and the applications the app writes.

The record of a document — what the Anlagenverzeichnis needs to name it — is always stored. The scanned file is stored only when you add one and agree to it. It then belongs to your account rather than to one phone, and deleting the account takes it with everything else.
Why: to produce the documents you asked for, which is the agreement between us — Art. 6 (1) (b) DSGVO. Nothing here is used for advertising and nothing is passed on for money.
The German is written by a language model outside this server: for that, and for nothing else, what you entered is sent to %1$s.
No language model is in use on this installation. What you enter is turned into German by rules on the server itself, and leaves it only in the file you export yourself.
Held until you delete the account. Deleting it takes your details, the documents on file, your postings and your applications with it, at once.

Your rights, Art. 15 to 21 DSGVO: to see what is held, to have it corrected, to have it deleted, to have its use restricted, to take a copy with you, and to object. Seeing it, taking it and deleting it are on the settings screen. You may also complain to a data-protection authority.
The particulars German law requires a service open to the public to state.
This installation has not said who operates it. Until it does, the Impressum the law asks for is missing, and the app must not be offered to the public.
